name: Twitch

maxWidth.note: 1080p60 standard; 1440p60 only via Enhanced Broadcasting (see enhancedBroadcasting).

portrait.note: Dual Format (vertical) via Enhanced Broadcasting is documented in the blog, but vertical resolution is not specified.

videoCodecs.note: H.264 for standard RTMP; HEVC only via Enhanced Broadcasting.

min.note: Not found in official pages reachable.

max.note: Standard RTMP cap. Enhanced Broadcasting is higher (see enhancedBroadcasting).

protocols.note: RTMPS confirmed live: every ingest entry's live API response carries both a plain template and a 'secure' template (same host, scheme swapped, no port — default 1935 plain / 443 secure). Resolves D148's open item (key previously went unencrypted in transit). The literal template strings live only under ingest.value (urlFormat / urlFormatSecure), per the URL-placement rule below.

multitrackVideo.note: Enhanced Broadcasting: client encodes multiple variants (Dual Format).

max.note: Not confirmed from an official page.

audioTracksMax.note: Not confirmed from an official page.

notes: Standard RTMP limits only. enhancedBroadcasting holds the higher limits for O5. Several audio/keyframe-adjacent fields still UNVERIFIED.

enhancedBroadcasting.note: Not used by Ujwalam until O5; never applied to the standard limits. Official blog agrees on 9 Mbps 1440p / 7.5 Mbps 1080p, HEVC for 2k: https://blog.twitch.tv/en/2026/06/17/introducing-dual-format-and-2k-streaming-on-twitch/

replyMaxChars.note: Send Chat Message: message limited to 500 characters (official reference).

ingest.note: Page: URL format "rtmp://<ingest-server>/app/<stream-key>"; the live ingests endpoint additionally gives url_template_secure ("rtmps://<ingest-server>/app/<stream-key>") for every server, same host. The user picks the server and stores its URL (now rtmps, same host as before) in Credential Manager (serverRef), so no server is hardcoded here.
